title: Small-batch coalescer miss case investigation
body:
Executive summary:

Observed repeated tail-latency spikes (~200-600ms extra per request) on production-like load when using the small-batch coalescer with FlashAttention enabled. Spikes correlate with high inter-request arrival variance and sequences that produce a lot of short microbatches (<=2 tokens). Preliminary traces show that these microbatches often fall through to unfused kernel paths or trigger extra kernel launches due to scheduler coalescing misses.

Why we care:
- Amplified p99 latency causes downstream application timeouts (customer incidents).
- Small microbatches increase per-token cost (GPU kernel launch overhead dominates).
- On H100/A100 pools, unfused kernels show 2x-5x slower throughput compared to fused FlashAttention path at typical seq-len distribution.

Hypothesis (short):
- The coalescer's time-window and sequence-length bucketing interact poorly with request interarrival variance, producing many microbatches that either: (a) do not meet the minimum coalesce size and are forwarded immediately, or (b) are dispatched but end up scheduled onto a GPU SM with no matching fused-op-ready microbatches, forcing a fallback kernel path.
- Additional factor: KV-cache warm-entry scheduling (paged attention) can delay the coalescer decision path when prefetch/populate is in-flight, causing decision jitter.

Experiment setup (replicable):
- Hardware: single A100 80GB (prod-like), single H100 (staging), multi-GPU runs for throughput experiments (4xA100).
- Runtime: latest serving-runtime branch HEAD (PR 4123 applied locally).
- Models: Llama2-13B (fp16), an internal 7B variant with fused attention kernels available.
- Workload generator: synthetic arrival stream that simulates PL/PG customer traffic with poisson, bimodal, and heavy-tailed interarrival distributions. Sequence lengths: 8–512, token generation behavior with spikes of 1–3 token replies.
- Coalescer knobs tested: window_ms {1,2,4,8,16}, max_coalesce_tokens {64,128,256}, bucket_timeout_ms {0,1,2}, enable_strict_bucket=true/false.
- Kernel toggles: flashattn=fused|fallback, fused-ops enabled/disabled, paged-attn prefetch=on/off, kv-prefetch-size {0,64,128}.
- Observability: nsight systems traces, NVTX regions injected in runtime, CUPTI kernel timelines, Triton-like per-request traces, custom microtrace (microbatch_id, arrival_ts, dispatch_ts, kernel_launch_ts, kernel_type).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 request latency, mean token throughput (tokens/s), kernel launch counts, average GPU SM occupancy, percent time spent in fused vs unfused kernels, count of microbatches <=2 tokens.

Key findings (high level):
1) Microbatch distribution matters more than global throughput. With heavy-tailed interarrivals, fraction of microbatches <=2 tokens rose from ~12% (poisson) to ~37% (realistic heavy tail).
2) When small-microbatch fraction >25%, fused-kernel utilization dropped by ~40% because the coalescer frequently emitted tiny batches that fell below internal thresholds for the FlashAttention fast-path.
3) FlashAttention path has higher fixed kernel-launch overhead but amortizes well for >16-token microbatches. For <=2 token microbatches, the fallback kernel (pointwise+attention-savvy path) is 3–5x slower per-token and incurs additional memory traffic producing the observed latency spikes.
4) Paged-attention prefetch sometimes blocks the coalescer decision path by holding the request in a reservation state for up to bucket_timeout_ms; when bucket_timeout_ms is tuned too high (>=8ms) we observed increased dispatch jitter and more singleton dispatches.
5) Fused-ops instability: occasional fallback to unfused ops was triggered by transient workspace allocation failures on A100 when memory fragmentation from many small allocations occurred. These correlate with periods of high small-batch churn.

Representative numbers (A100 single-GPU, synthetic heavy-tail):
- Baseline (window_ms=2, max_tokens=128, flashattn=fused): p95=78ms, p99=210ms, tokens/s=18k, fused_kernels=62%
- Aggressive coalesce (window_ms=8): p95=45ms, p99=110ms, tokens/s=25k, fused_kernels=83%
- Conservative coalesce (window_ms=1): p95=92ms, p99=350ms, tokens/s=12k, fused_kernels=41%
- Prefetch enabled + window_ms=2: p99 increased by ~40ms relative to prefetch off; increased reservation-held microbatches by 8%

Trace flavor example (microtrace snippet):
- request A: arrival_ts=0ms, coalesced with B (window_ms=2) -> dispatch_ts=2.4ms -> kernel_launch_ts=3.6ms -> kernel_type=flash-fused -> latency 45ms
- request C: arrival_ts=0.5ms, arrives alone (window expired) -> dispatch_ts=1.5ms -> kernel_launch_ts=4.2ms -> kernel_type=fallback-unfused -> latency 312ms

Root cause analysis (detailed):
- The coalescer uses a simple time-window + token-count heuristic that doesn't adapt to local interarrival variance. When arrival variance spikes, the window doesn't catch fast-but-bursting requests and either emits tiny batches or leaves requests waiting for prefetch.
- FlashAttention variants in our runtime require certain minimum contiguous token layouts and workspace allocation size to achieve the fused path. Tiny microbatches do not meet these constraints, forcing fallback.
- Paged-attention prefetch reservation creates a state machine where requests awaiting kv population are excluded from the coalescing pool until prefetch completes; if prefetched items are slow (remote storage / on-demand populates), the coalescer has fewer eligible requests and more singletons happen.
- Memory fragmentation: lots of small temporary allocations from many tiny microbatches increases GPU heap fragmentation which causes a small but meaningful fraction of fused-kernel launches to fail their workspace allocation and fall back. This is amplified by kernel retry logic which adds latency.

Mitigations tried (lab experiments):
- Increase coalescer window_ms to 6–8ms: reduces small-microbatch fraction, raises fused-kernel utilization, reduces p99 significantly for heavy-tailed traffic, but increases average waiting latency for strictly low-variance traffic patterns.
- Adaptive coalescing: implement a short-term estimator of interarrival CV (coefficient of variation) and expand window when CV high. Prototype reduced p99 by ~28% vs static 2ms in heavy-tail tests.
- Minimum microbatch padding: if coalescer emits <N tokens (e.g., 8), pad with dummy placeholders to meet fused path layout (requires kernel support). Prototype showed promise but increased compute slightly and required kernel changes.
- Reservation-aware coalescing: allow prefetched-but-pending requests to be tentatively coalesced with an expiration timer; upon prefetch completion adjust dispatch. Reduced reservation-induced singleton rate by ~60% (complexity trade-off exists).
- Aggressive workspace pooling: reuse a persistent workspace buffer per-stream to reduce fragmentation and allocation failures. Reduced workspace allocation fallbacks by ~75% in lab.

Recommended short-term actions (next 2–3 sprints):
1) Turn on adaptive coalescer (feature-flagged) in staging: implement interarrival CV estimator and adjust window_ms in [2,12] dynamically. (Owner: Rajat; Ticket INF-4726 backlog).
2) Implement workspace pooling in runtime allocator for attention kernels to shrink allocation churn. (Owner: Ethan; PR reference https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123).
3) Reduce bucket_timeout_ms default from 8 -> 2ms for paged-attention control plane; add a configuration parameter surfaced in Dedicated templates. (Owner: Priya).
4) Add telemetry: microbatch-size histogram, coalescer decision traces, workspace-failure counters, and fused-vs-unfused counters. Instrumentation ticket INF-4781.

Longer-term work (Q1 next year):
- Kernel-level support for padding small microbatches (or fast-path for length=1/2) to avoid full fallback; coordinate with serving-runtime <-> kerneldistro teams.
- Smarter prefetched-key backpressure: route requests that require slow prefetch to a separate coalescer queue tuned differently.
- Evaluating a hybrid coalescer that mixes time-window with model-aware token-cost heuristic (e.g., favor coalescing by expected decode tokens remaining).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How frequent are these heavy-tail arrival patterns in real customer traffic across different product features? Need longer-term telemetry to quantify.
- Are there pathological edge cases where aggressive coalescing increases p50 enough to break SLAs? Need product/CS input on latency SLO trade-offs.
- Interactions with autoscaling: if coalescing increases queueing slightly, autoscaler may react differently. We need a simulation to verify.

Action items / owners: (short)
- Rajat: adaptive coalescer prototype -> staging flag (due 2025-11-18) [INF-4726]
- Ethan: workspace pooling PR review and stress test (due 2025-11-12) [PR 4123]
- Priya: paged-attention timeout config change + rollout plan (due 2025-11-10)
- Maya (me): add microbatch telemetry dashboard + p99 alert baseline (due 2025-11-07) [INF-4781]

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a working analysis; numbers are from lab runs and synthetic generators. We need production traces and longer-running load tests before changing defaults globally.
- When reviewing the adaptive coalescer design, consider the simplicity/operational cost: added telemetry and knobs increase surface area. My recommendation is a conservative rollout behind a feature flag with tight telemetry and kill-switch.

Appendix: quick reproducibility commands
- start single-GPU harness: ./tools/harness --gpu a100 --model llama2-13b --coalescer window_ms=2,max_tokens=128,adaptive=false --arrival heavy-tail --clients 128 --trace microtrace.log
- convert nsight capture: nsys profile --output=cap --trace=nvtx ./runtime --config ...
- evaluate fused utilization: tools/trace-analyzer --input microtrace.log --metric fused_pct --bucket 1ms

Rough changelog of experiments (lab notes):
- 2025-10-02: initial observation in canary; triggered investigation
- 2025-10-08: gathered nsight traces, reproduced on A100
- 2025-10-15: ran memory pooling microbench; saw fragmentation correlation
- 2025-10-21: adaptive coalescer prototype v0.1; staging results promising
- 2025-10-28: stress runs across 4xA100 showed autoscaler stability when adaptive coalescer enabled

End of doc.
